interpretations: For each `order_item_id` and customer `town_city`, average non-null invoice-line `product_price` values and non-null line ratios `derived_product_cost / derived_total_cost`, following `Invoice_Line_Items → Invoices → Orders → Customers`. For each town, average those per-item price and ratio averages separately. Return towns whose town-level ratio exceeds the mean of the town-level ratios, showing the town, both town-level averages, and the difference from that cross-town mean, without rounding
queries:
WITH item_averages AS (
    SELECT
        ili.order_item_id,
        c.town_city,
        AVG(ili.product_price) AS item_price_avg,
        AVG(ili.derived_product_cost / ili.derived_total_cost) AS item_ratio_avg
    FROM Invoice_Line_Items AS ili
    JOIN Invoices AS i ON i.invoice_number = ili.invoice_number
    JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id
    JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    GROUP BY ili.order_item_id, c.town_city
),
town_averages AS (
    SELECT
        town_city,
        AVG(item_price_avg) AS town_price_avg,
        AVG(item_ratio_avg) AS town_ratio_avg
    FROM item_averages
    GROUP BY town_city
)
SELECT
    town_city,
    town_price_avg,
    town_ratio_avg,
    town_ratio_avg - (SELECT AVG(town_ratio_avg) FROM town_averages) AS ratio_difference
FROM town_averages
WHERE town_ratio_avg > (SELECT AVG(town_ratio_avg) FROM town_averages)
